newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chilean leader in Paris to boost ties.
newsitem.headline: Chilean leader in Paris to boost ties.

text.p: Chilean President Eduardo Frei began a four-day state visit to Paris on Wednesday, capping a spectacular strengthening of ties between France and the countries of South America's Mercosur economic powerhouse.
Chile is an associate of the fast-growing trade group.
Frei's trip came two weeks after French President Jacques Chirac toured the four Mercosur countries -- Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay -- and Bolivia, also a Mercosur associate.
Chirac has said he would visit all Latin American countries.

"I believe that...Chirac's initiative to seek a deepening of ties between the European Union and Chile, Mercosur and Latin America has a tremendous potential," Frei, who has been visiting Brussels this week, told Radio France Internationale.

Heads of state of South America's southern cone visited France last year. Chirac has blamed a delay in Frei's visit on schedule problems, denying suggestions it was a consequence of Chile's protests against French nuclear tests in the South Pacific.
The 1995-1996 tests halted a rapprochement which had started with the return of democracy in Chile in 1990 after 17 years of icy relations with the dictatorship of General Augusto Pinochet.
Frei told the daily Le Figaro Chirac's tour and his own visit heralded "a new vision of ties between France, a great pillar of development, and a Latin America engaged in strengthening democracy".
He supported Chirac's call, made during his South American tour, for a summit between Latin America and Europe and hoped the initiative would soon crystalise into a definite proposal.
Chile's first post-Pinochet, democratically-elected president, Patricio Alwyn, visited France in 1992. The previous visit by a Chilean president dated back to 1965, by Frei's father Eduardo.

Throughout his South American tour, Chirac emphasised the potential for boosting exchanges with France and with the EU, which signed a trade agreement with Mercosur two years ago and has already become its main trade partner.
French diplomats said Frei's visit would be an invitation to French business to invest in Chile, one of Latin America's fastest-growing economies.

France is currently the 10th largest investor in Chile, with French companies holding interests in public works, banking, telecommunications, insurance and wineries. Construction group Spie-Batignolles owns Chile's top ski resort, Valle Nevado.

Exchanges reached $950 million last year when Chile recorded a trade deficit with France for the first time this decade. Frei was expected to ask Chirac to ease trade barriers for Chilean exports, which Santiago blames for the deficit.

Frei's visit will also revive old cultural affinities which prompted many Chileans to seek asylum in France from Pinochet's 1973 coup. Frei told Le Figaro he would sign a cooperation accord on education.
